main_text.p: Διχοτομέω ὦ in duas partes feco. item sépàro. F. ἡσω, Matth.24.51. P. δεδιχοτόμηκα. a.1. ἐδιχοτόμησα.
Διψάω ὦ sitio.per metaph.fynecdochicam vehementer expeto. Fut. διψήσω. a.1. ἐδίψησα, Matth.25.42. P. δεδίψηκα.
Δίψα ὦ τὸ sitis, idem quod Th. δίψα ης ἡ, 2.Cor.11.27.

Δίψυχος ὁ ἡ (ex δὶς & ψυχὴ) animo duplex, Jac.1.8. claudicans in utrumq; latus, ut legimus 1.Reg.18.21. cor habens divisum, partim Deo, partim mundo deditum. Seu, qui alium animum lingua & gestibus prae se fert, alium vero intus habet. hoc est, qui est hypocrita.

Διώκω persequor. de re dictum, significat singulare studium ejus obtinenda, & vertitur sector: at de persona, notat nocendi cupiditatem. imperf. ἐδίωκον ες ε Johan.5.16. praes. imperat. διωκε ἔτω. Fut. διώξω. a.1. ἐδίωξα. a.1. act. imperat. διώξον ἔτω. aor.1.subj. διώξω ης η. praes.pass. διώκομαι perfecutione premor. prat.pass. δεδίωγμαι. a.1.pass. ἐδιώχθη. Fut.1. pass. διωχθήσομαι.
Δόγμα τος τὸ edictum, Luc.2.1. à δοκεῖ videtur, quod ita visum fuerit. δογματίζω ων τὰ ritus. Thema δοκέω.
Δογματίζω ritibus onero. Fut. ἰσω. P. δεδογματι[illegible, ~6 letters]

page.notes: The right-hand margin holds cut-off, cramped marginal notes (Greek and Latin references such as "Col.2.20", "Marc.10", "Rom.1.28", "Rom.14.18", "Luc.14.22") that are too damaged to read reliably; they are not transcribed. The final line of the main text is partly illegible. The main text lines are in italic and Greek type as printed, with some Greek readings doubtful.
